text: Project Aurora is an internal customer-support platform. The backend is built with FastAPI, memory is managed by Cognee, and the web client is served by Node.js.
Aurora uses a private memory dataset named private_memory. The application should keep memory retrieval scoped to this dataset and should never accept an arbitrary dataset name from the browser.
For local development, Cognee uses SQLite for relational state, LanceDB for vector search, and Kuzu for the knowledge graph. These stores are persisted under the project's backend/data directory.

Aurora runs Ollama locally for both the language model and embeddings. The configured embedding model is nomic-embed-text, and the application does not send memory content to OpenAI or another hosted LLM provider.
The memory lifecycle is remember for ingestion, recall for retrieval, improve for enrichment, and forget for deletion. A successful remember without a session creates permanent graph-backed memory.

The API should return only operation summaries for remember, improve, and forget. Recall results are returned only to an authenticated local caller; application logs must not contain request bodies or memory contents.
